subject.title: [Feature]: Cron should distinguish execution success from delivery failure and show warning instead of error

question: Should a successful cron execution with failed delivery become a first-class `warning` run status, or should cron keep execution `status=ok` and surface the delivery failure through delivery fields and warning UI?
rationale: Both open implementation paths address the misleading red execution failure, but they create different public API and persisted-state contracts that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use `ok` plus delivery fields
options.body: Land the narrower execution/delivery split, keep `CronRunStatus` stable, and make UI/operator surfaces render `lastDeliveryStatus=not-delivered` as a warning.

options.title: Adopt first-class `warning`
options.body: Proceed with the broader protocol/status expansion only with full Gateway, UI, docs, backoff, and external-client compatibility proof.

options.title: Keep current error semantics
options.body: Reject the split for now and continue treating failed required delivery as a primary cron run error.

recommendation.title: Use `ok` plus delivery fields
recommendation.body: Land the narrower execution/delivery split, keep `CronRunStatus` stable, and make UI/operator surfaces render `lastDeliveryStatus=not-delivered` as a warning.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-surface cron product/API decision involving runtime, protocol, UI, and compatibility behavior where steipete has the strongest recent ownership signal.
